info.bio: The Apples in Stereo son una banda de indie pop de Boulder, Colorado, asociada con el colectivo Elephant Six, un grupo de bandas entre las que inicialmente se encontraron Neutral Milk Hotel, The Olivia Tremor Control, Elf Power, The Minders o Beulah.  Actualmente cuentan con Eric Allen (bajo), John Hill (guitarra rítmica), y las nuevas incorporaciones de John Dufilho (batería), John Ferguson y Bill Doss (teclados), mientras que el cantante y guitarrista Robert Schneider escribe la mayoría de las letras y canciones de la banda.

scenes.name: Renacimiento pop, Elephant 6 y lounge-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En la primera mitad de los noventa el pop supera ampliamente a la música experimental: la revancha de la melodía tras un cuarto de siglo de sonidos progresivos. La vía más rentable sigue el pop barroco de los últimos Beach Boys, Van Dyke Parks, Big Star y XTC: Jellyfish (Bellybutton), Imperial Teen, Velvet Crush, Material Issue, Eggs, Fountains Of Wayne, Ben Folds Five, Chainsaw Kittens, Barenaked Ladies. El colectivo «Elephant 6» de Georgia y Luisiana es la escuela pop más influyente de la década: Apples In Stereo, Olivia Tremor Control, Neutral Milk Hotel (In The Aeroplane Over The Sea), Elf Power, Of Montreal; y sus herederos Ladybug Transistor y Photon Band. El folk-pop a lo Tom Petty y R.E.M.; el «lounge-pop» (Combustible Edison, Zumpano, Ivy, Cardigans, Squirrel Nut Zippers); el teen-pop (Hanson, Britney Spears, Backstreet Boys).

podcast.title: Financial Crisis of 1999
podcast.body: In the summer of 1999, the band's principals, Robert Schneider and Hillary Sydney (both 30), faced a severe financial bind. Both were working telemarketing jobs, and Hillary was eight months pregnant with their first child, which would prevent them from touring—a vital income source. They were concerned about affording their $825 monthly rent.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 2

podcast.title: Band Decision on Licensing
podcast.body: Despite their punk rock purist ethos, the $18,000 licensing offer for "Strawberry Fire" was more than the band could make in a year. When Robert and Hillary consulted the rest of the band, there was no hesitation, and the unanimous decision was to accept the money.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 2

podcast.title: Early Financial Struggles
podcast.body: As an indie band from Denver active since 1992, The Apples in Stereo were highly regarded within the indie community but struggled with album sales, typically moving only about 20,000 copies per record. To make ends meet, they toured frequently, playing around 100 shows a year, with gigs earning between $250 and $2,500. When not on the road, members took regular jobs, and t-shirt sales were minimal, bringing in around $100 per show.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 2

podcast.title: Ethical Dilemma over Licensing
podcast.body: The $18,000 offer for "Strawberry Fire" created an "existential crisis" for The Apples in Stereo, who had always adhered to the purist ethos of punk rock. They worried about compromising their artistic principles and disappointing fans who expected them to maintain that stance.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 2

podcast.title: Financial Rescue via Licensing
podcast.body: Accepting the $18,000 deal to license "Strawberry Fire" for a Sony TV commercial ultimately rescued The Apples in Stereo from a very difficult financial situation, proving to be a pivotal moment for the indie band.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 2

podcast.title: Sony TV Ad Offer
podcast.body: During their financial crisis in 1999, Robert Schneider and Hillary Sydney received a call from a friend at the ad agency Young and Rubikam in New York. The agency was working on a campaign for Sony televisions and wanted to use their song "Strawberry Fire," offering $18,000 for the license.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 2

xref.title: Peer Licensing Example
xref.body: Around the same time The Apples in Stereo licensed "Strawberry Fire" to Sony, Spiritualized, another fiercely independent band greatly admired by The Apples in Stereo, also made a licensing deal with Volkswagen, highlighting a growing trend among indie acts.

xref.title: Peer Licensing Example
xref.body: Around the same time The Apples in Stereo licensed "Strawberry Fire" to Sony, Stereolab, another fiercely independent band greatly admired by The Apples in Stereo, also made a licensing deal with Volkswagen, indicating a broader shift in strategy among indie musicians.
